mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of microscopic algae?
mcqs.explanation: Chlorella is a single‑celled green alga that can be seen only under a microscope. Kelp is a macroscopic seaweed, mushrooms are fungi, and Paramecium is a protozoan, so they are not microscopic algae.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that microorganisms have diverse roles
mcqs.question: Which statement best explains why microorganisms are considered to have diverse roles in the environment?

options.A: All microorganisms cause diseases in humans and animals
options.B: Some microorganisms produce oxygen, some decompose organic matter, some cause disease, and some are used in food production
options.C: Microorganisms only live in soil and have no function elsewhere
options.D: Microorganisms are only useful in laboratory research

mcqs.answer: Some microorganisms produce oxygen, some decompose organic matter, some cause disease, and some are used in food production
mcqs.explanation: Microorganisms perform many functions: photosynthetic algae produce oxygen, decomposers recycle nutrients, pathogens cause disease, and others like yeast help make bread and yogurt. Options A, C, and D are overly restrictive and incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches a group of microorganisms with a typical characteristic?

options.C: Protozoa – are unicellular eukaryotes that often move by flagella or cilia
options.D: Algae – are always multicellular and lack chlorophyll

mcqs.answer: Protozoa – are unicellular eukaryotes that often move by flagella or cilia
mcqs.explanation: Protozoa are single‑celled eukaryotes and many move using flagella, cilia, or pseudopods. Bacteria are prokaryotes (no nucleus), fungi are not photosynthetic, and algae can be unicellular or multicellular and contain chlorophyll.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise differences in their structures and habitats
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the structure and typical habitat of a group of microorganisms?

options.A: Bacteria are eukaryotic cells and live only in extreme environments
options.B: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin and are commonly found in soil and decaying organic matter
options.C: Algae lack chlorophyll and are restricted to desert soils
options.D: Protozoa possess peptidoglycan cell walls and are primarily found in hot springs

mcqs.answer: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin and are commonly found in soil and decaying organic matter
mcqs.explanation: Fungal cell walls contain chitin, and fungi thrive in soil, leaf litter, and other decomposing material. Bacteria are prokaryotic, algae contain chlorophyll, and protozoa do not have peptidoglycan walls; their habitats are varied, not limited to hot springs.
